questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used.

The drawing from an electron micrograph shows a ciliated epithelial cell, magnified ×1500, which is found in the trachea. Line X-Y shows the widest dimension of the cell. X Y What is the number of these cells that could be found along a 1cm length of the trachea?

Which row identifies the two solutions? boil with boil with add iodine Benedict’s add biuret Benedict’s solution solution after solution solution acid hydrolysis

Chitin is a polysaccharide consisting of long straight chains of the monosaccharide acetylglucosamine, linked by 1,4 glycosidic bonds. Acetylglucosamine is similar in structure to glucose, but contains nitrogen, allowing hydrogen bonds to form between adjacent chains of chitin when they lie parallel to each other. Which polysaccharide is most similar in structure to chitin?
Which statement about triglycerides is correct?

options.A: They are made up of three fatty acids combined with glycogen.
options.B: They are more saturated with hydrogen compared with phospholipids.
options.C: They form a bilayer in the cell surface membranes of cells.
options.D: They have a lower ratio of oxygen to carbon compared with carbohydrates.

Batrachotoxin is a poison found in frogs in the Columbian jungle. The poison is used by Native Indians to produce poison darts. The poison works by increasing the permeability of some cell surface membranes to sodium ions, which move out of the cells. Which statements are correct for cells affected by batrachotoxin?
Which processes occur during prophase of the mitotic cell cycle in an animal cell? centrioles chromosomes spindle fibres replicate condense form

The protein p53 is produced in a cell in response to DNA damage. This protein stops the cell cycle for a short time just before the DNA is replicated, so that the DNA can be repaired. At which phase of the cell cycle will this stop occur?

options.A: M B G1 C S D G2

questions.questionText: Which feature of stem cells enables them to replace cells in tissues such as the skin?

options.A: They are undifferentiated cells that are present at birth.
options.B: They differentiate to form skin cells.
options.C: They divide by mitosis to supply some cells that can differentiate.
options.D: They have the full number of chromosomes.

questions.questionText: DNA contains the ……X…… base ……Y…… which is joined to adenine with ……Z…… hydrogen bonds. Which row correctly completes the statement about DNA? X Y Z

CGCCGCACGCGC The table shows the amino acids coded for by 10 mRNA codons. mRNA codon amino acid AAG Lys ACG Thr CGG CGC CGU Arg CCG Pro GCC GCG Ala GGC Gly UGC Cys What is the order of the four amino acids in the polypeptide translated from this small section of a gene?

A student was asked to draw a plan diagram of the plant tissue shown in the photomicrograph and to annotate two observable features. What are correct annotations?

options.A: epidermis darkly stained layer of cells, xylem hollow vessels
options.B: epidermis formed of a single layer of cells, xylem strengthened by lignin
options.C: phloem small cells, xylem empty cells to transport water
options.D: vascular bundles arranged in a regular pattern, xylem large dead cells

questions.questionText: Water that is present inside a root hair cell may leave the cell and pass to the vascular tissue. Through which route must the water travel?
What is a correct definition of the term transpiration?

options.A: diffusion of water from intercellular air spaces to the atmosphere where it evaporates
options.B: evaporation of water from the leaf surface of a plant via the stomata
options.C: loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant to the atmosphere
options.D: movement of water from the xylem to the atmosphere through the cell walls only

questions.questionText: Which changes to the water potential and the volume of liquid in the phloem sieve tube element occur when sucrose is moved from a photosynthesising leaf into the phloem sieve tube element? water potential volume of liquid in phloem sieve in phloem sieve tube element tube element
Which statement supports the theory of active loading of sucrose into companion cells?

options.A: The pH decreases in the cell wall of the companion cells compared to the cytoplasm.
options.B: The pH decreases in the cytoplasm of the companion cells compared to the cell wall.
options.C: The pH decreases in the plasmodesmata between companion cells and sieve tube elements.
options.D: The pH decreases in the sieve tube elements compared to the companion cells.

questions.questionText: The diagram is an external view of the mammalian heart and the associated blood vessels. P Q R S Which statement about the blood vessels associated with a normal, healthy heart is correct?

options.A: P and Q carry blood with more oxyhaemoglobin than haemoglobin.
options.B: P and R carry blood that is saturated with oxygen.
options.C: S and P carry blood with a low oxygen concentration.
options.D: S and R carry blood with more haemoglobin than oxyhaemoglobin.

Which does not occur when a red blood cell arrives at the alveolus?

options.A: Carbaminohaemoglobin releases carbon dioxide from the α-globin and β-globin polypeptide chains.
options.B: Carbonic acid in the red blood cell forms carbon dioxide and water.
options.C: Hydrogencarbonate ions diffuse from the plasma into the red blood cell.
options.D: Hydrogen ions are released from haemoglobinic acid and diffuse out of the red blood cell.

questions.questionText: The graph shows the oxygen dissociation curves for haemoglobin of animals that live at high altitude and animals that live at low altitude. high altitude percentage saturation low of haemoglobin altitude with oxygen partial pressure of oxygen / kPa What explains the oxygen dissociation curve at high altitude?

options.A: Haemoglobin has a higher affinity for oxygen.
options.C: The change in partial pressure of carbon dioxide causes a Bohr effect.
options.D: The decrease in percentage of carbon dioxide causes the curve to shift to the left.

questions.questionText: Which statement concerning events that occur in the heart is correct?

options.A: As the wave of excitation passes through the atrioventricular node there is a time delay before it passes down the conducting fibres in the septum to the ventricles; this allows the atria to fill before ventricular systole.
options.B: Contraction of the ventricle muscles following atrial systole causes the ventricular blood pressure to rise above the blood pressure in the atria, closing the atrioventricular valve and preventing backflow.
options.C: The band of non-conducting fibres between the atria and ventricles prevents the wave of excitation from the atria reaching the ventricles directly; the wave of excitation passes to the Purkyne fibres and then to the atrioventricular node.
options.D: The primary pacemaker, the sinoatrial node in the left atrium, sends out a wave of excitation that spreads across the walls of the atria, resulting in the movement of blood from the atria into the ventricles.
